# COSTUME — Requirements

**Source of truth:** `REGISTERS.md` and `CONCEPT.md`. Every requirement below is derived directly from those documents. Do not edit this file to settle a design question — edit those documents first, then regenerate this one.

---

## Overview

**Everything arrives in costume. Paste a claim in and watch it undress.**

Given any public claim — product page, README, press release, AI model card, grant abstract — COSTUME shows, piece by piece, what the claim is *wearing* versus what it actually *paid for*. Detection is deterministic (a parser, not a model). The result is a single-page WebGL figure in the browser, no backend required.

---

## Hard Refuses (gate-enforced, non-negotiable)

These are enforced by `tools/gate_no_ecosystem_vocabulary.py`, which runs in `gate_cycle.sh` before any commit. Violating any of them is a build failure, not a review comment.

**HR-01.** This tool grades **documents only**. No surface, label, tooltip, placeholder, or example may score, rank, or rate a human being.

**HR-02.** No private-work vocabulary appears on the shipped page. The gate holds the list.

**HR-03.** The scope statement from §5 of `REGISTERS.md` is **visible in the UI on load** — not in a tooltip, not in a readme link, not in a comment.

---

## Functional Requirements

### Input

**FR-01.** The application provides a text area into which the user pastes any free-form text (a product page, README, press release, model card, grant abstract, or similar public claim document).

**FR-02.** The application processes the pasted text entirely client-side. No text is transmitted to any server.

### Parsing

**FR-03.** The parser splits input text into clauses by sentence boundaries and newlines. It must **not** split on `:` or `|`.

**FR-04.** Each clause is classified against all six registers independently. A clause may contribute to more than one register.

**FR-05.** Each clause is scanned for artifact tokens. Artifact scanning is per-clause, not per-document: an artifact three paragraphs away does not back a given sentence.

**FR-06.** The negation rule is applied: if a clause contains a negation word ("no", "not", "never", "without", "neither", "nor") that governs an artifact token, that artifact token does **not** count toward the artifact test. Negation does **not** suppress decline detection.

**FR-07.** The named-decline rule is applied: a decline counts only when it names what it declines. A bare refusal naming nothing is classified as HOLE, not DECLINED.

**FR-08.** The state resolver applies the priority rule per register: SOLID > DECLINED > COSTUME > HOLE.

### Register Detection

**FR-09.** The application detects and evaluates exactly six registers: WHO, WHAT, PROOF, PRICE, EDGES, RECHECK.

**FR-10.** Each register is assigned exactly one state: SOLID, DECLINED, COSTUME, or HOLE.

### Figure Rendering

**FR-11.** The application renders a single centre-screen figure in WebGL. The figure has six visible parts corresponding to the six registers (see Register Definitions below).

**FR-12.** Each figure part is rendered according to the state of its register (see State Definitions below).

**FR-13.** A RECHECK mirror figure is rendered to the right of the main figure, showing the RECHECK register state.

**FR-14.** On scroll, costume layers peel off one at a time from outermost (COSTUME state parts) inward. Parts in SOLID state remain.

### Scope Statement

**FR-15.** The following scope statement is rendered as visible UI text on page load, verbatim:

> This checks whether the evidence a claim needs is **present**. It does not judge whether that evidence is any good. A specification can be present and wrong and this will credit it.

---

## Non-Functional Requirements

**NFR-01.** Single page, client-side only. Zero server round-trips. No backend, no API key, no LLM call at runtime.

**NFR-02.** Deploys free on GitHub Pages. The submission must produce a live URL with no paid service required.

**NFR-03.** The parser is fully deterministic. Given the same input text it always produces the same RegisterMap.

**NFR-04.** The application is offline-capable once loaded (no runtime network calls).

**NFR-05.** The parser layer (all pure functions) is fully unit-testable without a DOM or canvas context.

**NFR-06.** The visual look (dark ground, single warm light source) uses named constants in the code, not magic numbers, so the aesthetic can be reproduced rather than tweaked.

---

## Register Definitions

These are drawn verbatim from `REGISTERS.md §1`. Acceptance criteria for each register are stated below.

### WHO — who is accountable

**Artifact:** a resolvable name — a person, a named organisation, an email, or a URL that identifies someone.

**Not an artifact:** "our team", "we", "experts", a logo alone.

**Figure part:** the mask.

### WHAT — what it does, bounded

**Artifact:** a verb plus a bounded object. Examples: "Converts PDF tables to CSV." "Runs on macOS 13 and later."

**Not an artifact:** adjectives without an object; a sentence whose only content is positive affect. If removing every adjective leaves nothing, the register is COSTUME.

**Figure part:** the costume body.

### PROOF — how you know

**Artifact (any one of):** a number with a unit; a dated measurement; a named benchmark, dataset, or test; a URL to a result; a reproducible command.

**Not an artifact:** "proven", "validated", "best in class", a customer count with no source, a percentage with no denominator.

**Figure part:** what the hands carry.

### PRICE — what it takes from the reader

**Artifact:** a figure with a unit (money, time, tokens, requests, seats), or an explicit "no cost" **with the terms that make it true**.

**Not an artifact:** "affordable", "free" standing alone, "starts at" with no number.

**Figure part:** the ground and shadow.

### EDGES — where it stops working

**Artifact:** a named condition, a stated bound, or an enumerated exclusion. Examples: "Not for real-time use." "Tested up to 10,000 rows." "English only."

**Not an artifact:** "some limitations apply". An empty EDGES register is the most common hole in real documents.

**Figure part:** the silhouette — crisp where stated, fraying where not.

### RECHECK — how the reader verifies it alone

**Artifact:** an imperative the reader can follow — a command, a reproduction step, a link to method, a downloadable sample.

**Not an artifact:** "contact sales", "request a demo", "read more".

**Figure part:** the mirror to the right of the main figure.

---

## State Definitions

These are drawn verbatim from `REGISTERS.md §2`.

| State | Condition | Visual treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **SOLID** | Named and carries an artifact | Lit, opaque, full weight |
| **COSTUME** | Named, no artifact | Translucent — fabric with nobody in it |
| **DECLINED** | Openly refused, and names what is refused | Absent, cleanly outlined, costs nothing |
| **HOLE** | Never mentioned at all | A gap, glowing at its edge |

**The distinction the whole thing turns on:** DECLINED is not a HOLE. A document that says "we do not publish latency numbers" has made a decision. A document that never mentions latency has a hole wearing the same clothes.

---

## Parser Rules as Acceptance Criteria

### AC-P1: Negation Rule

Fixture: `"We publish no latency threshold"`

Expected: the token "threshold" does **not** count as a PROOF artifact. The clause must not cause PROOF to resolve as SOLID or COSTUME. (It may contribute to DECLINED if the named-decline rule is also satisfied.)

Rationale: the clause contains the artifact signal but the negation word "no" governs it. Crediting it would let a document's own confession of absence score as presence.

### AC-P2: Named-Decline Rule

Fixture A: `"We make no claims"` → must classify as **HOLE**, not DECLINED.

Fixture B: `"We do not measure retention"` for EDGES register → must classify as **DECLINED**.

Rationale: "We make no claims" names nothing specific. "We do not measure retention" names what it declines. The gate is the named object, not the negative phrasing.

### AC-P3: Clause-Splitting Rule

Fixture A: `"Latency: under 12ms"` → must remain a **single clause** (no split on `:`).

Fixture B: `"Format | CSV, JSON, Parquet"` → must remain a **single clause** (no split on `|`).

Rationale: splitting on `:` or `|` severs the register keyword from its own artifact. A correct clause-splitter preserves these; an incorrect one makes every well-documented page score worse than a vague one, inverting the entire result.

---

## Out of Scope

The following are explicitly not part of this application:

- No backend of any kind (server, serverless function, database).
- No LLM or model call at runtime or build time for parsing decisions.
- No scoring, ranking, or rating of persons — only documents.
- No authentication, accounts, or persistent storage.
- No paid third-party services required to run or deploy.
- No WebGL unit tests or headless canvas testing — the render layer is visual-inspection only.
